items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: Benny Goodman hired Teddy Wilson to play as a member of the first Goodman trio

ctx.x: But it doesn’t matter. And the great breakthrough came about in the middle 30s when Benny Goodman hired Teddy Wilson to play as a member of the first Goodman trio that started on records actually. But Goodman decided we’re going to do this in person. So what he did was to play a set and maybe twice an evening, they would do this at the end of the set there would be a brief break and out would come the trio with Teddy replacing Jess Stacy on piano and Gene Krupa returning to the drums, and they would play maybe…
It wasn’t just in the south either, was it?

items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Carl Bellinger was the nephew of Mildred Bailey. He’s the one whose drum set was in Mildred and Red Norvo’s house when Benny Goodman and Teddy Wilson were visiting.

ctx.x: Oh, Marshall spotted it right away, yeah. That broke everybody up. I’ll never forget that. I mentioned the other people that came over to Marshall Stearns were not students. Mainly it was two people. One was Sammy Goodman, who was a local tenor saxophone player who admired Bud Freeman and Lester Young. The other was Carl Bellinger. There was still another. Carl Bellinger was the nephew of Mildred Bailey. He’s the one whose drum set was in Mildred and Red Norvo’s house when Benny Goodman and Teddy Wilson were…

early age at a time when it was very unusual to go cross country. The other attraction was that one of my cousins had moved out to California, in Pasadena, and married a California girl. So I could visit there also. As a kind of a by-product, I became the godfather of their little girl, who had just been born a little while before.
